schema.description: scenario_renderer: one scenario's synthetic evidence packet (quarantined: spec I4).
schema.title: PacketDraft

request.system:
You render one abstract fuzzing scenario as a synthetic evidence packet: the documents a resolver would see in a world
where exactly that scenario holds. The packet is synthetic and quarantined (it never stands as real evidence), and its
purpose is to test whether a contract's prose resolves as its formal representation does. So the packet must make the
scenario's assignment recoverable from the documents alone, as real records would, and nothing else.

You are given the contract's observables and sources, and the scenario: the value of each atomic condition (true or
false), the published values it fixes (a measurement on a day, a publication date, an instrument's terms), and its
stress class where it has one (conflicting sources, a revised value, a renamed or recodified instrument, partial scope,
a stay or injunction, evidence missing at expiry).

Write one to four documents, each with a title, the issuing source (one of the contract's sources, or a source the
scenario names), a publication date and time with its zone, and the text: an enrolled-bill excerpt, an agency notice, a
station data table, an order. Write them as such records are written, in their register and format. Every condition the
scenario fixes is established, or left unestablished where the scenario says it is unknown, by what the documents say.
Do not state the contract's outcome, mention the contract, or explain the scenario. Do not add facts that would bear on
any other condition of the contract; where a document must mention something incidental, keep it neutral.

documents.text:
CF BENCHMARKS LTD
INDEX OPERATIONS – INCIDENT NOTICE

Index affected: CF Ethereum Real-Time Index (ERTI), ticker ETHUSD_RTI
Incident reference: OPS-2026-1101-03
Status: Investigating

At approximately 22:51:20 UTC on 1 November 2026, the calculation engine for the CF Ethereum Real-Time Index stopped disseminating index values. The interruption is linked to a fault in the ingestion of order book data from constituent exchanges. Dissemination resumed at approximately 23:07:45 UTC.

No ETHUSD_RTI values were published for the interval 22:51:20 UTC to 23:07:45 UTC. Values disseminated for this interval through data feeds, the website and the API show as null.

Index Operations is reviewing whether the index can be recalculated for the affected interval from archived constituent data, in line with the CF Benchmarks Methodology Change and Exceptional Event Policy. Clients should not treat any value for the affected interval as published until CF Benchmarks issues a further notice.

A further update will follow.

CF Benchmarks Index Operations
indexops@cfbenchmarks.com
documents.title: Incident Notice: CF Ethereum Real-Time Index (ETHUSD_RTI) – Calculation Interruption

CF BENCHMARKS LTD
INDEX OPERATIONS – INCIDENT UPDATE

Incident reference: OPS-2026-1101-03
Index affected: CF Ethereum Real-Time Index (ETHUSD_RTI)
Status: Under review – no restatement issued

This update follows the notice of 1 November 2026 about the interruption to ETHUSD_RTI dissemination between 22:51:20 UTC and 23:07:45 UTC on 1 November 2026.

Index Operations has finished its initial review of archived constituent data for the affected interval. Data from one or more constituent exchanges for part of the interval could not be fully validated. The matter has been referred to the CF Benchmarks Oversight Function.

As of this update, CF Benchmarks has not published any recalculated or restated ETHUSD_RTI values for the affected interval. The interval stays NULL in all CF Benchmarks data products. CF Benchmarks cannot yet say whether or when values for the interval will be published.

CF Benchmarks will announce any decision on the affected interval through a further notice.

CF Benchmarks Index Operations
indexops@cfbenchmarks.com
